direct_answer:
Yes. Equinor discloses that it has an Energy transition plan (ETP), first published in 2022 and updated in 2025, which sets out ambitions and actions to support its net-zero ambition for 2050 and is integrated into business planning and approved by the board and CEO. [Source 4][Source 2][Source 3]

On 1.5°C alignment: Equinor states that its target to reduce net operated (scope 1+2) emissions by 50% from 2015 to 2030 is “consistent with a science based, 1.5℃-aligned trajectory as defined by IPCC pathways,” and also states these targets “align with the lower end of IPCC 1.5°C-consistent pathways.” [Source 2][Source 5] However, the retrieved passages do not provide the ESRS E1-4 level detail on the methodology/framework used to assess 1.5°C compatibility (beyond referencing IPCC pathways), nor external assurance of targets.
compliance_rationale: Evidence clearly confirms the existence of a climate transition plan (ETP), including governance (board/CEO approval) and integration into strategy and planning. [Source 4][Source 2][Source 3][Source 1] Evidence also includes an explicit claim of 1.5°C alignment for a key scope 1+2 target and a statement that targets align with IPCC 1.5°C-consistent pathways. [Source 2][Source 5] But the retrieved passages do not include the full ESRS E1-4 disclosures needed to substantiate 1.5°C compatibility (e.g., specific framework/methodology, underlying scenarios for target-setting, and whether targets are externally assured).
disclosure_gaps: Framework/methodology used to determine that GHG targets are science-based and compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C (beyond general reference to IPCC pathways).
Underlying climate and policy scenarios used specifically for setting the GHG emission reduction targets (not just for portfolio resilience testing).
Whether the GHG targets (and/or transition plan) have been externally assured.

Clear explanation (by reference to GHG targets) of how the overall transition plan (including value chain aspects) is compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C; retrieved evidence focuses mainly on operated scope 1+2 and provides limited substantiation for value chain alignment.
key_findings: Equinor has an Energy transition plan (ETP), first published in 2022 and updated in 2025, setting out short- and medium-term ambitions/actions to support a net-zero ambition for 2050. [Source 4]

The ETP is integrated into business planning and is developed/reviewed/updated in consultation with and approved by the board of directors and the CEO; progress is reported annually. [Source 2][Source 3]

Equinor states an operated (scope 1+2) emissions reduction aim of 50% from 2015 to 2030 and claims this pace/scale is consistent with a science-based, 1.5°C-aligned trajectory as defined by IPCC pathways. [Source 2]
Equinor also states that these targets align with the lower end of IPCC 1.5°C-consistent pathways. [Source 5]
